title: Fusion traffic cut
caption: A chain of k elementwise kernels round-trips an N-element tensor of B-byte values per kernel: each of the k ops reads and writes the full buffer. One fused kernel reads once and writes once. For the LayerNorm + dropout + activation chain (k = 3) the idealized traffic cut is ~3x, before counting the k - 1 launches it also removes.

symbols.name: unfused traffic
symbols.meaning: total buffer bytes moved when each op in the chain is its own kernel

symbols.name: fused traffic
symbols.meaning: buffer bytes moved by the single fused kernel

symbols.name: chain length
symbols.meaning: number of elementwise or normalization ops fused into one kernel

symbols.name: element count
symbols.meaning: elements in the tensor the chain operates on

symbols.name: element width
symbols.meaning: bytes per element (4 for FP32, 2 for FP16)

symbols.name: one round-trip
symbols.meaning: one full read plus one full write of the N-element, B-byte-per-element tensor

title: Dispatch overhead law
caption: N_op dispatched operations each pay a fixed host cost o; the device owes t_compute + t_memory under the additive no-overlap model. When R exceeds 1 the accelerator waits on Python. Every lever is named: fusion and capture shrink N_op, graph replay shrinks o, a larger batch grows the denominator. Dispatch share of step time is R/(1 + R).

symbols.name: overhead ratio
symbols.meaning: host issue time divided by ideal device time; above 1 the step is dispatch-bound

symbols.name: operation count
symbols.meaning: dispatched operations in one step (the MNIST step models 5 Python entries, 9 driver launches)

symbols.name: per-op host cost
symbols.meaning: Python dispatch plus kernel-launch overhead per operation, ~15 us in the chapter's illustrative model

symbols.name: compute time
symbols.meaning: device time at the peak rate for the step's FLOPs

symbols.name: memory time
symbols.meaning: device time at memory bandwidth for the step's modeled traffic

symbols.name: host issue time
symbols.meaning: total software time to dispatch and launch the step's operations

title: Compilation benefit
caption: P production executions each save (t_eager - t_compiled); the setup cost is one compilation plus D development recompilations. Above 1 the capture pays for itself. The book's cost model puts the eager-to-JIT crossover near 2x10^6 executions and JIT-to-AOT near 6.7x10^6; ResNet-50 serving at ~47% speedup breaks even near 135K images.

symbols.name: production executions
symbols.meaning: inference requests or training steps the compiled artifact will serve

symbols.name: development iterations
symbols.meaning: code changes that each force a recompilation

symbols.name: eager time
symbols.meaning: per-execution time with op-at-a-time dispatch

symbols.name: compiled time
symbols.meaning: per-execution time of the captured or exported artifact

symbols.name: compile time
symbols.meaning: cost of one compilation or recompilation, assumed constant

symbols.name: per-run saving
symbols.meaning: time recovered on each execution after compiling

title: Saved-activation memory
latex: A \approx B_{\text{batch}} \cdot L \cdot S \cdot d \cdot k \cdot e
caption: Each of the L layers saves about k tensors of B x S x d activations at e bytes per element until the backward sweep unwinds past it. Linear in batch and depth; a non-sequence model drops S, a conv net replaces S x d with feature-map H x W x C. This is the term that makes the ResNet-50 training peak 82-121x its weight storage.

symbols.name: saved memory
symbols.meaning: bytes of forward activations retained for the backward pass

symbols.name: batch size
symbols.meaning: samples per step; scales the retained tensors linearly

symbols.name: depth
symbols.meaning: layers that each hold saved tensors until backward reaches them

symbols.name: sequence length
symbols.meaning: token positions per sample; absent for non-sequence models

symbols.name: width
symbols.meaning: hidden dimension (feature-map H x W x C in conv nets)

symbols.name: tensors per layer
symbols.meaning: count of forward values each layer's backward rule must read

symbols.name: element width
symbols.meaning: bytes per stored activation element

title: The Jacobian reverse mode never builds
caption: A Jacobian for a 100,000-by-100,000 map has 10^10 entries - 40 GB in FP32, larger than most models. Reverse mode instead propagates adjoints as vector-Jacobian products from the scalar loss: every gradient in one backward sweep at a small constant multiple of forward cost. Forward mode would need one sweep per input direction.

symbols.name: Jacobian
symbols.meaning: matrix of every output's derivative with respect to every input

symbols.name: Jacobian shape
symbols.meaning: outputs by inputs; 10^10 entries for the 100K-wide pair

symbols.name: entry width
symbols.meaning: bytes per FP32 derivative

symbols.name: materialized cost
symbols.meaning: why no framework materializes J: it would not fit beside the model

symbols.name: vector-Jacobian product
symbols.meaning: what reverse mode actually computes per node - the adjoint times the local Jacobian, as a small matrix-vector product

title: Dense backward work
caption: Each dense layer's backward runs two forward-sized GEMMs (the weight gradient and the input gradient), except the first layer, whose input gradient nobody requests. For the 784->128->10 step the dense training work is ~2.013x the forward - ch5's three-product rule with its input-gradient exception applied.

symbols.name: training dense work
symbols.meaning: total GEMM MACs in the forward plus backward passes

symbols.name: forward dense work
symbols.meaning: MACs of the forward dense layers

symbols.name: three-product rule
symbols.meaning: forward GEMMs plus two backward GEMMs per layer

symbols.name: first-layer exception
symbols.meaning: the input-gradient GEMM for layer 1, omitted because the raw input needs no gradient

symbols.name: worked ratio
symbols.meaning: the 784-128-10 step's actual dense multiplier once the exception is removed

title: Adam step traffic
caption: FP32 Adam reads p, g, m, v and writes p, m, v: seven values at four bytes each per parameter. For the 101,770-parameter MLP that is ~2.85 MB - more traffic than the entire modeled forward-plus-backward step, and the term small training loops forget to count.

symbols.name: optimizer traffic
symbols.meaning: bytes moved by one Adam update step

symbols.name: values touched
symbols.meaning: reads of p, g, m, v plus writes of p, m, v

symbols.name: value width
symbols.meaning: bytes per value, 4 in FP32

symbols.name: parameter count
symbols.meaning: trainable weights (101,770 for the worked MLP)

symbols.name: Adam state
symbols.meaning: parameter, gradient, first moment, second moment

title: Dispatch share of step time
caption: The fraction of step time the host spends issuing work. R = 15.7 for a 1-us kernel gives 94% - the eager gantt's idle gaps made quantitative. R = 0.15 for a ~100-us GEMM gives 13%. The same per-op cost is everything for small ops and nothing for large ones.

symbols.name: dispatch fraction
symbols.meaning: portion of total step time spent in Python dispatch and launches

symbols.name: overhead ratio
symbols.meaning: host issue time over ideal device time, from the dispatch overhead law

symbols.name: step total
symbols.meaning: device time plus host issue time, normalized to device time

symbols.name: worked ends
symbols.meaning: small-op and large-op dispatch shares in the chapter's model
